findings: The repair deletes the stale lower-numbered Connect duplicate and relies on ADR-0131/ADR-0132 already merged for Connect expansion and Connect core public contracts.
The OP-11 and hyperscaler-pattern decisions are renumbered to ADR-0133/ADR-0134 because the earlier range is reserved for inherited compatibility IDs and Oyatie numbering gaps.
Accepted/required enforcement claims were downgraded to proposed planning contracts until validators, workflows, branch-protection rows, and integration tests exist.
The portfolio hyperscaler backlog remains explicit, but no product is allowed to claim maturity from ADR-0134 alone.
Workflow Studio golden-signal language now distinguishes latency, traffic, errors, and saturation from availability SLOs.
Branch-protection and required-check claims are bounded to future validator PRs instead of asserted by this docs repair.
The primary failure mode was circular aspirational enforcement: ADRs claimed missing lanes as required while later lanes cited those ADRs.
The repair makes that circularity impossible for PR #135 by using planned validator identifiers and proposed ADR status.
